newsitem.title: USA: Lucent CFO defends accounting policies.
newsitem.headline: Lucent CFO defends accounting policies.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc Chief Financial Officer Don Peterson on Monday defended his company's accounting practices as conservative, saying an analyst report questionning the telephone equipment maker's accounting as wrong-headed.

Peterson did not identify the analyst, whose report hurt Lucent's shares, but Smith Barney last week questionned Lucent's method of accounting for revenues and whether or not it had sufficient financial reserves for some of its businesses.
"There was a whole lot of inference and not a lot of fact," Peterson said at an investor's meeting sponsored by Raymond James & Associates Inc.
Lucent has the most conservative methods for recognizing revenues among all makers of equipment for a new generation of wireless telephony called personal communication system (PCS), Peterson said.
He said Lucent recognizes PCS revenues in its accounts only when it has fully implemented a fully operating PCS system, while rivals recognize revenues earlier.
"We have the most conservative accounting of PCS revenue in the industry."
The executive also said Lucent had adequate reserves.
"We think we are very solid in our reserving," he said.
